title: Compare deltas per dollar invested, not per contract
summary: A 50 delta option has more gamma than a 20 delta option per contract. But for the same money you buy several 20 delta options, and the net gamma is much higher. The cost is theta: if the move does not come quickly, the low delta position decays faster. If you are unsure of the timing, the speaker prefers 40 to 50 delta.

params.label: 20 delta contracts
params.help: About the same cost as one at-the-money call.

steps.caption: The stock trades at $100. We compare one 50 delta call with about the same money in 20 delta calls.
One 50 delta call: more gamma per contract, but only one contract.
Four 20 delta calls cost about the same. Their curve bends much more on a fast move: more net gamma.
The difference grows with the size of the move. This is the convexity you buy with low delta.
The catch is theta. If the move does not come quickly, the 20 delta position decays toward zero.
The low delta position needs a bigger move to break even at expiry.

takeaways: Per contract, a 50 delta option has more gamma than a 20 delta option.
For the same money, 20 delta options carry much more net gamma.
Low delta options lose more to theta if the move is slow.
With an uncertain time frame, 40 to 50 delta balances gamma and theta.
caveats: Strikes and contract counts in the chart are example values; the transcript gives none. Betting on earnings is an event trade.
